newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks expected to inch ahead in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks expected to inch ahead in cautious trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to inch ahead on Tuesday, pursuing their attempt to regain lost ground after reaching six-month lows last week, but analysts said investors remained cautious.

"The market is cautious but probably biased on the upside. The overseas market performed well so investors will bargain hunt at this level," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
The Hang Seng Index rose 83.25 points to 12,287.84 on Monday. Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London gained 22.61 points to 12,310.45.
Overnight, the Dow industrials rose 29.84 points to 6,555.91.
Vickers Ballas sales director Antony Mak said while he expected a rebound, there were really no incentives to be in the market. "Most of the money will stay on the sidelines," he said.
So said the market had gone down so much that investors were not convinced the current decline was over. "There is no good news to drive the market significantly higher," he said.
The Hang Seng blue chip index touched a low of 11,951.24 points last week, a level not seen since early October 1996.
